{{Short description|Complex in algebraic topology}}

[[File:Cech-example.png|thumb|Constructing the Čech complex of a set of points sampled from a circle]]

In [[algebraic topology]] and [[topological data analysis]], the  '''Čech complex''' is an [[abstract simplicial complex]] constructed from a point cloud in any [[metric space]] which is meant to capture [[topology|topological]] information about the point cloud or the distribution it is drawn from. Given a finite point cloud ''X'' and an ''ε''&nbsp;>&nbsp;0, we construct the Čech complex <math>\check C_\varepsilon(X) </math> as follows: Take the elements of ''X'' as the vertex set of <math>\check C_\varepsilon(X) </math>. Then, for each <math>\sigma\subset X  </math>, let <math> \sigma\in \check C_\varepsilon(X) </math> if the set of ''ε''-balls centered at points of σ has a [[empty set|nonempty]] [[intersection (set theory)|intersection]].  In other words, the Čech complex is the [[Nerve of a covering|nerve]] of the set of ''ε''-balls centered at points of ''X''. By the [[Nerve of a covering|nerve lemma]], the  Čech complex is homotopy equivalent to the union of the balls, also known as the [[offset filtration]].<ref name = ghrist>{{Cite book|title=Elementary applied topology|last=Ghrist|first=Robert W.|date=2014|isbn=9781502880857|edition=1st|location=[United States]|oclc=899283974}}</ref>

==Relation to Vietoris–Rips complex==
The Čech complex is a subcomplex of the [[Vietoris–Rips complex]]. While the Čech complex is more computationally expensive than the Vietoris–Rips complex, since we must check for higher order intersections of the balls in the complex, the nerve theorem provides a guarantee that the Čech complex is homotopy equivalent to union of the balls in the complex. The Vietoris–Rips complex may not be.<ref name = ghrist/>
